summary: Dune strategy entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: Dune II
entries.definitive_edition: MS-DOS original via original hardware or DOSBox with owned data

emulation.notes: Document DOSBox version, cycles, sound device, and source of game data.

primary.version: Dune II: The Building of a Dynasty via owned DOS release/DOSBox
primary.why: Dune II is a foundational RTS artifact and the MS-DOS release is the core route. There is no clean modern storefront definitive edition, so the archive route should use owned original data with DOSBox or document a preservation/open-source engine route separately.
primary.how_to_play: Use an owned DOS copy in DOSBox or original DOS hardware. Record version/title variant, DOSBox version, cycle/sound settings, house chosen, difficulty/mission route, save state, and whether Amiga/Genesis or OpenDUNE/Dune Legacy were compared.

secondary.platform: Genesis / Mega Drive Dune: The Battle for Arrakis
secondary.what_to_play: Use if documenting the console adaptation.
secondary.why: It changes interface/control assumptions from the DOS RTS route.

secondary.what_to_play: Use only if original data/source and engine state are clearly documented.
secondary.why: They are preservation tools, not original release artifacts.

all_releases.fidelity: Computer ports with platform-specific presentation differences.
Console adaptation with different interface and controls.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Original DOS fidelity conflicts with convenience/source-port routes and console adaptations.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record version/title variant, DOSBox settings, house/mission route, and any source-port use.

entries.title: Dune 2000
entries.definitive_edition: Original Windows release with all cinematics and conservative compatibility fixes

emulation.emulator: Original Windows environment, Wine, or a Windows 98 virtual machine
emulation.notes: Prefer the original engine with owned data. GruntMods can supply compatibility tooling, but optional campaigns and missing movie packs must be documented rather than silently mixed into the base run.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Windows campaign and movies with stable modern capture.

primary.version: Original Windows campaign with its movie files and a documented compatibility patch
primary.why: The Windows release has the original 2D presentation, mouse controls, full three-House campaign, and live-action mission movies. Use the original engine for the main run because OpenRA explicitly rebuilds and rebalances the game rather than reproducing it unchanged.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally owned Windows CD installation, retain the movie files, and apply only a documented modern-Windows compatibility patch or launcher. If using GruntMods tooling, verify that the original campaigns and all cinematics are installed and record every optional component.

all_releases.fidelity: Original 2D engine, mouse interface, multiplayer, three campaigns, and live-action movies.
all_releases.reason: primary: fullest original-engine capture and control route.

all_releases.fidelity: Console conversion using a different 3D engine, with cheats, link-cable multiplayer, and PlayStation Mouse support.
all_releases.reason: skip: largely the same story and gameplay, but a weaker control and presentation route than PC and no verified exclusive campaign content.

all_releases.fidelity: Modern open-source rebuild with gameplay, effects, interface, and difficulty changes.
all_releases.reason: skip for the archival main run: excellent modern strategy route, but not behaviorally identical to the 1998 game.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: OpenRA is easier to run and improves modern usability, but it changes gameplay and campaign difficulty. The original Windows engine is less convenient yet remains the content and behavior authority.

entries.remaster_caveats: There is no official modern remaster or current digital purchase route. OpenRA is a reimplementation with deliberate gameplay changes, and the PlayStation port replaces the PC's 2D engine with a 3D one.
